summary: Refactored waitForKey() to call enterRawMode() instead of inlining raw-mode setup — removed readline import from screen.ts
Added TTY guard to clearScreen() — early return when !process.stdout.isTTY, making it a no-op in CI/piped environments
Created tests/screen.test.ts with 7 tests covering both changes (TTY and non-TTY paths)
All 101 tests pass, tsc --noEmit is clean

comments.note: screen.ts is now a clean thin wrapper over raw-mode.ts — no code-quality issues in the touched files.
The readline import in screen.ts was the only direct coupling between screen.ts and Node's readline module; removing it keeps the module's dependency surface minimal.

summary: All 3 acceptance criteria verified against source and test output.
Build check: tsc --noEmit exits clean (no errors).
Full regression suite: 105/105 tests pass — no regressions.
AC1 confirmed: screen.ts has no readline import; waitForKey() delegates entirely to enterRawMode() from raw-mode.ts.
AC2 confirmed: clearScreen() has `if (!process.stdout.isTTY) return;` guard — no-op for false and undefined.
AC3 confirmed: 7 new tests in tests/screen.test.ts cover TTY and non-TTY paths for both clearScreen() and waitForKey().

comments.note: tests/screen.test.ts uses Object.defineProperty to set isTTY values. vi.restoreAllMocks() does not revert Object.defineProperty mutations — only spies are restored. Each test re-defines the value it needs before executing, so no test-order dependency exists in practice. Consider adding an afterEach that resets isTTY to its original value via Object.defineProperty for extra robustness.

enterRawMode() in raw-mode.ts has a secondary isRawModeSupported() guard plus a try/catch, providing a defensive safety net beneath screen.ts's outer stdin.isTTY check. This layered approach is good defensive design.

summary: PASS — both changed files reviewed line-by-line across all four review dimensions.
screen.ts: clean, minimal, SRP upheld. clearScreen() TTY guard correctly handles false and undefined. waitForKey() delegates entirely to enterRawMode() with no residual readline coupling.

tests/screen.test.ts: seven well-structured tests across two describe groups. vi.spyOn on rawMode namespace is the correct Vitest ESM pattern. process.stdin.once mock ensures synchronous promise resolution without real TTY.
raw-mode.ts: not modified but reviewed for delegation integrity. try/catch in enterRawMode() and restoreTerminal() provides a solid safety net below screen.ts's outer isTTY guard.
No blocking issues. No Fix-Forward edits applied. Two documentation-forward items tagged (stale README Phase B callouts). One low-priority robustness observation echoing QA.

comments.note: [documentation-forward] README.md §clearScreen() has a stale 'Phase B hardening' callout stating the isTTY guard is 'planned for Phase B'. The guard is now implemented — update the callout to describe the actual behavior: clearScreen() is a no-op when process.stdout.isTTY is falsy.

[documentation-forward] README.md §waitForKey() has a stale 'Phase B hardening' callout stating process.stdin.setRawMode(true) is not wrapped in try/catch. This is no longer true — waitForKey() now delegates to enterRawMode() which contains the try/catch. Update or remove the callout to reflect the current implementation.

tests/screen.test.ts — afterEach calls vi.restoreAllMocks() which restores spies but does not revert Object.defineProperty mutations on process.stdout.isTTY / process.stdin.isTTY. In practice this is harmless because every test sets the value it needs before executing, so no test-order dependency exists. For future resilience, consider capturing the original isTTY values in beforeAll and restoring them in afterEach.

notes: All three acceptance criteria verified. screen.ts no longer imports readline — enterRawMode() from raw-mode.ts handles all raw-mode setup. clearScreen() has an explicit isTTY guard. New tests/screen.test.ts covers both functions across TTY and non-TTY paths using vi.spyOn — no real TTY required.
